slides.0.title: Winemaking II: second fermentation, ageing and disgorgement
slides.0.subtitle: From tirage to dosage
slides.1.title: Tirage and second fermentation
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Timing and ingredients
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Tirage may begin only from 1 January after the harvest; the wine receives a liqueur de tirage (sugar, yeast and riddling agent)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Glass bottle, new materials
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Second fermentation takes place only in glass bottles; bottles and closures must be new (specification); temporary closure is usually a crown cap or cork
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Pressure and residual sugar
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Pressure is about 5–6 bar (6 bar at 20°C, Comité Champagne); the specification requires fermentable sugars (glucose plus fructose) ≤ 10 g/L after prise de mousse
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Textbook values
slides.1.highlights.3.content: About 4 g/L of sugar gives 1 bar, so roughly 24 g/L adds about 1.2–1.3% alcohol (as in Level 1; textbook approximations, not specification text)
slides.1.content: Sugar and pressure at tirage are concepts: learn the direction, not the decimals.
slides.2.title: Lees ageing and autolysis
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Three timing rules
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Disgorgement may not occur before 12 months after tirage (the wine staying in bottle without interruption); NV is released no earlier than 15 months and Vintage no earlier than 36 months after tirage
slides.2.highlights.1.title: On the lees versus from tirage
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Comité Champagne's factsheet words 15 and 36 months as ageing on the lees, while the INAO text says from tirage and separately requires disgorgement after at least 12 months; the course follows the specification and does not test the wording difference
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Autolysis
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Compounds released as dead yeast breaks down add brioche, toast and almond notes and a finer mousse, more so with time (a trend, not a hard number)
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Most go well beyond the minimum
slides.2.highlights.3.content: The Comité notes most producers age longer than the minimum; if wine is returned to bulk and re-bottled (remise en cercle), the minimum period restarts from the new tirage date
slides.2.content: The legal period is only a floor; flavour is set by the actual time on lees.
slides.3.title: Riddling and disgorgement
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Remuage
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Done by hand on a pupitre or by machine in a gyropalette, it gradually gathers the lees in the neck
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Dégorgement
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The neck is frozen into an ice plug and the bottle's pressure expels plug and lees when it is opened; the specification counts by-products of disgorgement at about 0.5% of the volume
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Sold in the bottle it was made in
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Champagne must be finished and sold in the bottle of the second fermentation; only formats under 75 cl or over 150 cl may be transferred, using an isobaric system
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Disgorgement date
slides.3.highlights.3.content: The INAO labelling clauses do not appear to require a disgorgement date; some producers print it voluntarily so drinkers can judge time on lees and time since disgorgement (concept)
slides.3.content: Remuage solves where the lees sit; dégorgement solves how to take them out.
slides.4.title: Dosage: the last style decision
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Liqueur d'expédition
slides.4.highlights.0.content: After disgorgement a liqueur d'expédition of wine and sugar is added, setting final sweetness and style
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Seven categories (g/L)
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Brut Nature <3 (no added sugar); Extra Brut 0–6; Brut <12; Extra Dry 12–17; Sec 17–32; Demi-Sec 32–50; Doux >50 (EU rules, Comité Champagne FAQ)
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Tolerance
slides.4.highlights.2.content: A tolerance of ±3 g/L means neighbouring categories overlap; boundary values are not tested, only the order of categories and what Brut Nature means
slides.4.highlights.3.title: The volume formula
slides.4.highlights.3.content: The volume added by the liqueur d'expédition is capped: V(%) = 1.266 × A + 0.0666 × S, where A is the rise in alcohol (% vol) and S the rise in sugar (g/L)
slides.4.content: In order: Brut Nature, Extra Brut, Brut, Extra Dry, Sec, Demi-Sec, Doux.
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge check
How soon after tirage may disgorgement take place under the specification?
Specification: disgorgement not before 12 months after tirage; 15 and 36 months are the minima before release.
A. More than 50 g/L of sugar
Brut Nature is the driest category with no added sugar, under 3 g/L.
Which step gathers the lees in the neck of the bottle?
Remuage gathers the lees in the neck, after which dégorgement expels them.
